reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as instruction about legal online earning methods, including commerce, affiliate, tutorial, freelance, and shoutout workflows. It includes conditions and disclosures such as parental permission and optional affiliate commissions. The described monetization advice, platform-workaround suggestion, webpage banner offer, and subscribe graphics do not establish a deceptive request for money, credentials, or financial participation by the video itself.

citations.quote: I'm gonna be showing you five different ways to make money online for free
All you need to do is sign up for a free CafePress account
Method two, make money by creating YouTube tutorial videos
Every time someone buys, say Adobe Premiere or Photoshop through an affiliate link, you will get 85% of the first month of the subscription.
you also place a link to where people can go and buy your video course that you are selling through Teachable.

opening.argument: The pitch repeatedly ties accessible viewer actions to income: create a free merch account and list products, publish tutorials with affiliate links, or offer services. The clearest low-barrier example is registration for a free online merch store, with the promised payoff being commission when a customer buys. For teenagers, the video also gives routes around payment barriers, including bank accounts or mailed checks. That is a concrete action-to-cash solicitation, even though the video does not establish that every viewer will earn.

citations.quote: All you need to do is sign up for a free CafePress account
when a customer buys the product, Cafe Press will collect their money and remove the product creation fees from it and send the rest to you as profit in the form of a commission
CafePress will let you get your commissions mailed to you in the form of a check

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling these workflows educational does not erase their sales structure: the viewer is invited to register, create listings, and pursue commissions. The disclosure that affiliate links are optional addresses whether the presenter earns a commission, not whether the video’s repeated income promise may induce viewers to act. Nor does describing a check payout establish how likely earnings are for an ordinary beginner.

citations.quote: Using affiliate links is optional but again, it enables me to keep making my YouTube tutorial content free
People are making hundreds to even thousands of dollars a month selling merchandise like this on these online marketplaces

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An action linked to possible income is not by itself evidence of a scam. The merch explanation specifies that a customer must buy before a commission exists, and the description identifies affiliate links and commissions openly. The video presents several ordinary work-for-sale routes; these excerpts do not show a guaranteed reward, a payment demanded from viewers, or a deceptive claim that registration itself produces cash.

citations.quote: when a customer buys the product
Please note: an affiliate link tracks whether you click on the link, and register and/or make a purchase. If you do, I may get a commission.

opening.argument: The risk signals accumulate: the headline promises “FREE Money,” the speaker stresses that methods need no startup money, and the tutorial cites striking earnings, including hundreds or thousands monthly from merch and substantial income from a single day of reselling. It then directs viewers toward external platforms and ways to receive payouts. Those claims can make a low-effort, low-risk opportunity sound unusually accessible, especially to teenagers. The evidence does not prove the figures false, but the promotional combination warrants skepticism about the implied ease and representativeness of the returns.

citations.quote: 5 Ways To Make FREE Money
none require a Paypal account or any start up money
People are making hundreds to even thousands of dollars a month selling merchandise like this
I ended up making over $1,000 for just one day of flipping

rebuttal.rebuttal: The existence of conditions and disclosures does not answer the central concern: exceptional-sounding earnings are paired with beginner-oriented instructions and prompts to act. The cited examples are not accompanied here by evidence of typical results, while the speaker directs viewers toward external services and affiliate-linked offerings. The audience can reasonably hear a stronger earnings prospect than the caveats establish.

citations.quote: there are tons of successful case studies, like this 1 on the internet, for you to read and watch if you just take a second to Google it
FREE ECOMMERCE EBOOK

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are framed as examples and possibilities, not guaranteed returns: the speaker says viewers can try methods and describes earnings from particular sellers or personal experience. A customer purchase is required for merch commissions, and the video explains that platform fees are deducted before payout. External links and an income topic do not establish that the presenter is deceptively acquiring viewers’ money or assets.

citations.quote: all of these ideas are things that you can try
Cafe Press will collect their money and remove the product creation fees from it
there are tons of successful case studies

opening.argument: The instructional format also functions as a funnel into participation. Viewers are walked through specific platforms and payout mechanisms, directed to a free ebook and related resources, and invited to follow an Instagram account. The video’s own description prominently offers business tools through affiliate links and says a commission may result from clicks followed by registration or purchase. So this is not detached discussion of online income: it promotes actions and services while using accessible-earnings instruction to motivate engagement. That commercial framing supports treating its income claims cautiously.

citations.quote: FREE ECOMMERCE EBOOK
If you do, I may get a commission.
I get a commission on that sale
go ahead, check out my next video

rebuttal.rebuttal: The fact that the subject is instructional does not make the commercial elements incidental. The presenter explains affiliate commissions, directs viewers toward linked resources, and teaches ways to monetize content and services. The defense’s emphasis on optional links may clarify disclosure, but it does not negate that the video’s income narrative can steer viewers toward participation and commercial platforms.

citations.quote: WHOLESALE TED AFFILIATE LINKS
I went ahead and I put that affiliate link in my video description

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Commercial promotion is not equivalent to a scam. The description explicitly states that affiliate links are optional and that a commission may be earned; the spoken example likewise explains that commissions follow a purchase. The video describes business workflows and platform participation, but these excerpts do not show a concealed payment demand, guaranteed earnings, or an attempt to take viewers’ funds.
